name: Caminho do Mar (Via Ferrata dos Pinheirinhos)
coordSource: ferrataguide.com parking point (route start given there as 38.4321, -9.1456); OSM point 38.4302, -9.1348 lies ~1 km east
approach: Drive from Sesimbra toward Zambujal de Cima, then along Rua dos Almocreves to a small parking area. Walk dirt tracks toward the sea, then descend to the cliff with the help of fixed ropes. Allow 40–45 min.
features: Sea-cliff traverse above the Atlantic, very exposed, sparsely equipped, fixed ropes on the approach, sea views throughout
access: Free to self-guide; guided trips from about €45–65
operator: No managing body found; guided by Vertente Natural (vertentenatural.com) and sold via Manawa
kitRental: Vertente Natural includes harness and helmet in the trip price; no standalone rental found
season: Operators run it year-round; no official closure periods found
summary: A short but airy coastal via ferrata on the limestone cliffs west of Sesimbra, with the ocean directly below. The equipment is sparse and the approach is tricky to find, so it suits people who already have some experience.
facts: Total about 2 h 25 min: 40 min approach, 1 h on the route, 45 min back
Length disagrees: 430 m equipped (RocJumper, 2025) vs 800 m (ferrataguide)
The approach descends steeply with fixed ropes; a GPS track helps
No photo URL verified

name: Fenda da Arrábida via ferrata and abseil circuit
coordSource: No source gives coordinates. The OSM point 38.4547, -9.0161 could not be matched to this site.
approach: Guided only. Meet at Praia do Creiro (Portinho da Arrábida), then a short van transfer to the Fenda.
features: A 700 m geological fissure; via ferrata sections, abseils of 10–30 m, a cave passage, sea views over Portinho
access: Guided only; from €40 per person on Manawa
operator: WIND (Praia do Creiro) and Discover The Nature (Portinho da Arrábida)
kitRental: All equipment is included in the guided price
summary: A guided adventure circuit through a 700 m rock fissure inside Arrábida Natural Park, mixing short via ferrata sections with abseils and a cave. It suits beginners more than a classic self-guided via ferrata does.
facts: 4 h guided activity, minimum age 8 (WIND)
No public, self-guided route found
Coordinates and length are unknown for the equipped sections; 700 m is the length of the fissure
Your OSM #1 is still unverified; it may be a misplaced Pinheirinhos entry

name: Caminho sobre o Oceano Ordovícico (Via Ferrata da Serra do Muradal)
coordSource: Route start N39°56.802 W007°45.831, from the Caminhantes Wikiloc sheet quoting climbingportugal; matches OSM 39.9454, -7.7635
grade: K2 (RocJumper 2025) / A/B (via-ferrata.de); officially 'algo difícil' (≈K3); OSM says B
approach: From the EN238 near Estreito, take the dirt road signed 'Parque eólico do Pinhal Interior' to a saddle with an info panel. Follow the GR38 path to the base of the rock, about 10–20 min.
features: Staples on quartzite ridges, no bridges, wide views over the Muradal crest, part of the GR38 Pangeia route
operator: Município de Oleiros with Naturtejo Geopark; guided trips by Epic Land (epicland.pt, bookable via bookinxisto.com)
kitRental: Epic Land includes equipment in its €80 trip; no standalone rental found
season: All year (Caminhantes); the area burned some years ago and is regrowing
summary: Portugal's second via ferrata (2015), a short, staple-only climb on quartzite ridges in the Naturtejo Geopark. It's a good first via ferrata, and the views over the ancient folded ridges are the highlight.
facts: About 2 h total: 20 min approach, 1.5 h route, 10 min back
Grade sources disagree, from A/B to K3; most recent (RocJumper 2025) says K2
Height: 75–90 m equipped, about 150 m total ascent including approach
No warning signs at the start, so put your helmet on during the approach

name: Via Ferrata da Serra das Talhadas
approach: From Catraia Cimeira take the M1313 toward Chão do Galego. Start at the watchtower designed by Álvaro Siza Vieira, then walk about 800 m (20 min) to sector 1. The circuit ends back at the tower.
features: Circular traverse in 11 sectors, a 15 m Himalayan bridge, a 40 m suspension bridge, ladders, views over the Ocreza valley
operator: Município de Proença-a-Nova; guided trips by Epic Land (epicland.pt)
kitRental: Epic Land includes equipment in its guided trips; no standalone rental found
season: The municipality says not to use it in bad weather or at very high fire risk
summary: The longest via ferrata in Portugal, a ridge circuit with two bridges in the Naturtejo Geopark. It reopened in 2026 after repairs from the 2023 wildfires.
facts: Reopened mid-2026 after fire damage; it was listed as temporarily closed before that
Length disagrees: 2,190 m total (municipality) vs 1,400 m (2021 press)
The municipality recommends going with experience or with a guide
One person at a time on the Himalayan bridge, two on the suspension bridge

name: Via Ferrata do Rabaçal (Ecovia do Rabaçal)
coordSource: Visit Alto Tâmega e Barroso tourism page GPS (41.685917, -7.215806), at Barreiros; matches OSM 41.6865, -7.2149
approach: Park on Rua Principal in Barreiros, by the cemetery and festival square. Walk down past a viewpoint to the river beach, then follow signs to the panel at the start. The loop is about 4.4 km.
features: Granite wall above the Rabaçal river, a slightly overhanging section, an optional Tibetan/Himalayan bridge (~20 m) at the end, a river beach nearby
operator: Município de Valpaços; guided trips by Azibeiro House Nature (€30, minimum 3 people)
kitRental: Azibeiro includes PPE in its €30 trip; no standalone rental found
summary: The only via ferrata in Trás-os-Montes, climbing a granite slope above the wild Rabaçal river, with an optional cable bridge at the top. It pairs well with the Ecovia walking trails and the river beach.
facts: Circular walk about 2 h 15 min in total (Wikiloc track)
Grade sources disagree, from K2 to K3; the steepest section is slightly overhanging
Opened in 2019–2020 as part of the Ecovia do Rabaçal
Barreiros is 16 km from Valpaços; your OSM note says ~22 km from Chaves

name: Via Ferrata do Barranco do Demo
coordSource: ferrataguide.com route start; OSM 'North Slope' point 37.3289, -8.4884 is ~350 m west
grade: K1 (RocJumper) / A (ferrataguide); a Wikiloc user rates it a very easy K2
approach: Drive to Alferce and follow signs to the Passadiços do Barranco do Demo; parking is near the cemetery. The via ferrata starts off the walkways, about 5 min away.
features: A small suspension bridge, handrails, gorge views, combines with the walkways and their 50 m suspension bridge
access: Unknown; the walkways are free to visit
summary: A short, very easy via ferrata from 2025, built off the Barranco do Demo walkways near Alferce. It makes a good family add-on to the walkway hike.
facts: About 30 min on the route plus 5 min each way
I couldn't find the OSM name 'North Slope' in any source
No managing body, fee, or kit rental found; check with Câmara de Monchique
Opened 2025 (Wikiloc track description)

name: Via Ferrata da Penha (Senhora da Penha)
coordSource: Route start 39.411088, -7.464491 from the Caminhantes Wikiloc sheet
approach: Park at the Ermida de Nossa Senhora da Penha car park above Castelo de Vide. Follow yellow dots downhill to the base of the cliff, about 10 min. Return by the chapel stairs.
features: Gneiss cliff, a short negatively-sloping traverse, views over Castelo de Vide, finishes at the hermitage
operator: Câmara Municipal de Castelo de Vide with CIMAA (Alentejo Feel Nature); guided trips by GreenRoc (greenroc.pt) and via GetYourGuide
kitRental: Guided trips include equipment; no standalone rental or price found
season: All year (Caminhantes); the area was recently burned
summary: A short beginner route built in 2015 up the cliff below the Penha hermitage, with wide views over Castelo de Vide. The sideways traverses are the most technical part.
facts: About 45 min: 10 min approach, 30 min climb, 5 min back
Length disagrees: 160 m (RocJumper) vs 200 m (via-ferrata.de, Caminhantes)
Third via ferrata built in Portugal
GreenRoc minimum age is 14

name: Via Ferrata da Barragem de Santa Luzia
approach: Park at the foot of the Santa Luzia dam (Casal da Lapa) and walk to the west wall, about 2 min. Return over the dam or via the viewpoint on the N344.
features: 5 sections, vertical slabs, several slightly overhanging passages, ledges, ladders, dam and reservoir views
operator: Município de Pampilhosa da Serra with Aldeias do Xisto; guided trips by Epic Land
kitRental: Epic Land guided trip from €90, equipment included
season: Shaded in the morning, in sun in the afternoon; no official closures found
summary: Portugal's hardest via ferrata, a short but strenuous climb up the granite wall beside the Santa Luzia dam. It's for experienced people with good arm strength.
facts: Duration disagrees: about 1.5 h total (RocJumper) vs about 2.5 h (ferrataguide)
Several overhanging sections make it strenuous; not for beginners
Go in the morning for shade

name: Via Ferrata da Pombeira (Pombeira Adventure Park)
grade: C (ferrataguide, viaferrata.pt); mostly B to B/C with a C finish
approach: Park at the Pombeira Adventure Park near Lamelas / Codeçais, then walk about 30 min to the start. The return to the car is short.
features: River-canyon route along the Pombeiro, three bridges (Himalayan/Tibetan/monkey, 9–40 m), waterfalls, ends at a suspended viewpoint
access: Unknown whether the park charges entry; guided €25–70 depending on operator and group size
operator: Município de Castro Daire (Pombeira Adventure Park); guided by Latitude 41, Zona Canyoning, GreenTrekker and others
kitRental: Latitude 41 €55–70 with kit; Zona Canyoning €45; viaferrata.pt €35; GreenTrekker €25 without kit or €40 with
season: Very little shade, so avoid hot summer middays
summary: Often called the most complete via ferrata in Portugal, it follows a granite gorge with waterfalls and crosses three cable bridges. The park was officially inaugurated in 2026 after years of delays.
facts: About 2.5 h: 30 min approach, 2 h route, 5 min back
Length disagrees: 750 m (operators) vs 1,560 m (ferrataguide)
It was closed to the public from late 2023 until the park's official opening in 2026
Bridge descriptions vary between sources

name: Via Ferrata da Póvoa de Lanhoso (Monte do Pilar)
grade: K2 officially, feels like K1 (ferrataguide) / A/B (via-ferrata.de)
approach: Drive up Rua do Pilar and park at the lower bend near the base of the monolith. The start is about 2 min away; walk down by road from the castle afterwards.
features: Granite monolith, staples, short traverses, ends at Lanhoso castle and the Pilar sanctuary; optional double abseil down
kitRental: DiverLanhoso includes kit (via ferrata plus double abseil, €24)
summary: Portugal's first via ferrata (2012), a short beginner climb up the country's largest granite monolith to Lanhoso castle. It is private, so you must book through DiverLanhoso.
facts: Signs at the start forbid using it without the operator
Directories report the cable isn't properly fixed at the anchors, and via-ferrata.de says it is no longer maintained
Length disagrees: 70 m (ferrataguide) vs 150 m (RocJumper, via-ferrata.de)

name: Via Ferrata Teto do Mundo
approach: Take the M520 southeast from the Alto Rabagão dam to the first farm, where a sign marks the access. Follow the fence and faint yellow arrows, about 10 min.
features: Suspension bridge, ladders, rocky summit, viewpoint at the Teto do Mundo GIAHS observatory
operator: Município de Boticas; guided outings have been run by Boticas Hotel Art & Spa and CEITA Montalegre
season: It closed briefly after a 2021–22 wildfire; no other closure info found
summary: A short climb to a rocky summit viewpoint in the Barroso highlands, with a suspension bridge along the way. It's an easy add-on to a visit to the Barroso area.
facts: Status disagrees: listed as closed by Ferratas Hierro y Roca (2024), but RocJumper found it OK in 2025
Reopened by the municipality in March 2022 after fire damage to the bridge
Duration disagrees: about 55 min (RocJumper) vs about 80 min (ferrataguide)

name: Via Ferrata de São Vicente (planned)
coordSource: None; announced only as near the São Vicente Clube Naval
approach: Planned on the coastal cliff next to the Clube Naval in São Vicente
features: Announced with steel cables, staples and suspension bridges, and sea views
summary: In January 2022 the municipality announced Madeira's first via ferrata, a 280 m coastal route budgeted at about €150,000. I found no evidence it has been built.
facts: Announced January 2022; no construction or opening news found since
A Madeira guide's site still describes it as only being planned
No coordinates, grade or opening date available
No via ferrata found in the Azores either
